about: A tool that turns Android apps back into readable Java code, so people can study how an app works.

prs.title: Comparing boxed numbers keeps its meaning
prs.broken: Two boxed numbers compared with == were shown as a plain number compare, which gives a different answer.
prs.changed: The decompiler now keeps them boxed in that compare.
prs.matters: The decompiled code behaves like the original.

prs.title: Joined text uses the right variables again
prs.broken: In decompiled Java, text joined after a large number pulled in the wrong variables, so the output said something the app never did.
prs.changed: The decompiler now reads each piece from the right place.
prs.matters: Decompiled code matches what the app really prints.

prs.title: Calls that take any number of values keep their meaning
prs.broken: Some Java methods take any number of values. When an app passed one empty value or one list, the rebuilt code dropped a wrapper, so the method got something different and could crash.
prs.changed: The tool now keeps the wrapper in exactly those cases, so the call means what it did in the app.
prs.matters: Rebuilt code behaves like the original app instead of quietly doing something else.

prs.title: Joined text no longer turns into a sum of numbers
prs.broken: Code that glued two numbers into text, like 1 and 2 into "12", came back from the tool as adding them, giving 3. The rebuilt code meant something different from the app.
prs.changed: The tool now keeps the text joining when the first two pieces are numbers, matching what the app really does.
prs.matters: People reading the rebuilt code see what the app actually does, not a quietly wrong version.

prs.title: Adding empty text to a single value now stays text
prs.broken: Code that turned a letter or number into text by adding empty text came back from the tool without the empty text. The rebuilt code returned a number where text was expected and would not compile.
prs.changed: When the only piece being joined is not text, the tool now keeps the empty text in front, so the result is still text.
prs.matters: Rebuilt apps compile again and mean the same thing as the original code.
